svg.title: Generate and submit the final new-key CSR — instructional mockup
svg.desc: Step-specific guided recreation. Not a genuine screenshot or live result.
svg.text: INSTRUCTIONAL MOCKUP — NOT A LIVE CAPTURE OR RESULT
Generate and submit the final new-key CSR
Application server (TLS-APP01) · RHEL 9 Bash terminal · learner@10.90.0.10
RHEL 9 — learner@tls-app01
COMMAND / FILE CONTENT TO ENTER — PRESERVE CASE
sudo sh -c 'umask 077; test ! -e /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v4.key && openssl req -new -newkey
rsa:3072 -noenc -sha256 -keyout /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v4.key -out /home/learner/tls-
work/app-v4.csr -config /home/learner/tls-work/req.cnf'
sudo chown root:root /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v4.key
sudo chmod 600 /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v4.key
sudo chmod 644 /home/learner/tls-work/app-v4.csr
sudo restorecon -v /etc/pki/tls/private/app-v4.key
openssl req -in ~/tls-work/app-v4.csr -noout -verify -subject -text
scp ~/tls-work/app-v4.csr learner@10.90.0.20:~/tls-ca/incoming/app-v4.csr
EXPECTED RESULT / SIMULATED CLUE — CHECK YOUR OWN MACHINE
A valid app-v4.csr reaches the CA and app-v4.key stays protected locally.
FOLLOW THE NUMBERED INSTRUCTIONS IN THE LESSON
1. Paste the guarded newkey block. The private key remains under /etc/pki/tls/private.
2. Inspect the CSR signature and SAN. Submit only after those checks pass.
3. Copy the CSR to the separate practice CA. No public-service enrollment occurs.
No real private key, real certificate result, production access or DoD endorsement is shown.
